Subject: MerchantX: request to accelerate tenant-affinity + prompt-windowing (urgent)

Hi Rishi / Laura —

Quick heads-up on MerchantX (MX). They verbally committed to an expansion to our Dedicated offering last week; legal fast-tracked contract redlines but procurement has one firm technical prerequisite before signing: tenant-level prompt-windowing (ability to bind prompt meshes to a tenant affinity token, plus a short retention TTL) and a lightweight tenant affinity shim so their traffic is pinned to their regional pool. They say this is a blocker for their compliance team.

Attached is the requirements doc MerchantX sent this morning (merchantx_requirements_v1.pdf) and an initial MAP from CS. High level asks:
- Tenant affinity token support (per-request header + sticky routing for 30m)
- Prefix/prompt-windowing that prevents cross-tenant KV cache leakage
- Minimal observability hooks: request id + tenant id in traces

They need a go/no-go from Product/Eng by EOD Friday so procurement can finish up next week. This is a $1.2M ARR expansion in year 1 and they are willing to sign a short-term EAP if we can ship a limited-scope solution quickly.

Can you advise on feasibility and an ETA for a minimal safe path? If we need to trade off functionality, please propose the smallest ship that keeps the deal viable.

If helpful, Sonia (MerchantX) is available for a 30-min tech sync tomorrow.

—Stephanie

Subject: Re: MerchantX: request to accelerate tenant-affinity + prompt-windowing (urgent)

Stephanie — thanks for the clear ask and the spec. Quick reaction from Eng: we can approach this two ways with rough effort estimates and risk profiles.

Option A — "shim + guardrails" (fast, limited scope)
- Implement a tenant-affinity header that pins routing to a tenant pool (sticky session via router) + a TTL (30m).
- Add per-tenant prefix isolation for KV cache lookup to prevent cross-tenant hits (logical prefixing, minimal changes to runtime).
- Emit tenant_id on existing traces.
Estimated effort: 2 engineers x 2-3 sprints (4–6 weeks) with a high chance of meeting a short EAP; low infra churn. Known risks: subtle cache boundary bugs if clients use unexpected prefixes — needs strong test harness and a canary.

Option B — "full tenancy layer" (robust, longer)
- Full tenant-aware routing, stronger guarantees for residency and strict per-tenant KV namespaces, schema & policy enforcement.
Estimated effort: 3–4 engineers x 2 months (8–10 weeks). Better long-term but misses MerchantX procurement timeline.

Edge case we should call out: MerchantX asked for a near-term retention TTL and proof of isolation for SOC-type auditors. For Option A we can instrument an export that demonstrates per-tenant trace separation, but SOC team may push for more formal controls later.

Next steps I recommend: 1) decide if Product is willing to accept a timeboxed EAP with Option A, 2) if yes, allocate a 2-engineer squad for a 6-week rush + dedicated SRE for canary, 3) schedule a short tech sync with Sonia to confirm assumptions.

I can draft an engineering risk summary for the prioritization meeting.

—Rishi
